exposure: early feeding patterns (exclusively/predominantly mother's own milk [MAINLY-MOM])
mother's own milk supplemented with fortified donor human milk (MOM + DONOR)
mother's own milk supplemented with preterm formula (MOM + FORMULA)
outcome: in-hospital growth (growth rate, head growth, overall weight gain)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 1,272 preterm infants born at less than 32 weeks' gestation, categorized as extremely preterm (<28 weeks) and very preterm (28 to <32 weeks).
finding: While supplementing mother's own milk with fortified donor human milk or formula showed no difference in short-term growth, length of stay, or neonatal morbidities, early feeding primarily with mother's own milk was associated with significantly lower overall weight gain compared to supplementation with donor human milk.
followup_time: Until hospital discharge, with specific growth velocity analysis over the first 30 days of life and from regaining birth weight to discharge.
gest_age: Less than 32 weeks (extremely preterm <28 weeks; very preterm 28 to <32 weeks)
